name: half-denormal-results-of-arithmetic-and-conversions
rationale: The Metal side of the D57.12 half-denormal case: specified in D57.12, never authored until now. D57.1 rounds every half result with OpQuantizeToF16, which may flush a result below the smallest normal half to either signed zero. That is F16DenormFlush, whose comparison class D113 derives, with D57.12's Vulkan column as its test. D110.6 observed Metal keeping a half denormal from a bfloat conversion (word 45 of wide-convert-and-math-leftovers, a2995080, Q1's one remaining mismatch). Inputs are D57.12's: a = 0x0001, 0x8001, 0x0400, 0x0003, 0x03FF, 0x0400, 0x03FF, 0x0001, 0x83FF, 0x0001; b = 0x3C00, 0x3C00, 0x3800, 0x3800, 0x0001, 0x03FF, 0x4000; w = 0x33C00000, 0x33000000, 0x33000001, 0x387FC000. Words 0..11 are the rows h[0..11] zero-extended, and words 12..13 are f[0..1]. D57.12 names two output buffers; a case observes one, so they are joined. The module is compiled -fno-fast-math, so no nsz is on the results that are zero. Expected, from IEEE binary16 with nearest even and denormals kept: 0x0001, 0x8001, 0x0200, 0x0002, 0x0400, 0x0001, 0x07FE, 0x0002, 0x0000, 0x0001, 0x03FF, 0x0001, 0x33800000, 0xB87FC000. The observation also shows whether Metal keeps half denormals in arithmetic, which that column assumes.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-twenty-four-simd-primary
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 24 and receives exact float4 zero from all twenty-three linked _uber_clear bodies. A twenty-six-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. The entry writes that result to the poisoned primary texel before subgroup aggregation, and binding zero is captured byte-exactly.

name: manual-float4-fetch-at-an-offset-transformed-onto-three-of-four-pixels
rationale: Reaching variant of this entry's manual-vertex-fetch case (TODO 6.2, WP-RVC), whose zero constants gave a degenerate position. Constant 132 enables manual fetch; table slot 0 holds the same-library callback re::vertexfetch::fetchFromFloat4, and record 0 of the vertex-argument buffer (15 records of 24 bytes, the rest null) points at float4 positions with stride 16 and offset 16, which skips a leading decoy vertex (40, 40, 40). The three positions are (-1, -1), (3, -1), (-1, 3) with z = 1/4 with the matrix z scale 2, so world z = 5/8. The instance matrix (objectToCrWorld, column-major) scales x and y by 1/2, scales z and translates by (-1/4, -1/4, 1/8); crWorldToProjArray[0] keeps x, y and w and maps z to z/2 + 1/16, so the clip triangle is (-3/4, -3/4), (5/4, -3/4), (-3/4, 5/4) at w = 1. It covers the pixel centres (-1/2, 1/2), (-1/2, -1/2) and (1/2, -1/2) of the 2x2 target with a margin of at least 1/4 from every edge and misses (1/2, 1/2): pixel (1, 0) keeps its fill. The depth is the same at all three vertices, so its interpolation is exact; every product and sum is a small dyadic value, exact in float with or without contraction, and the observer writes (x + 1/2, y + 1/2, z, 1) for each covered pixel. This entry applies no depth bias (screenSpaceDepthBias = 1/4 is authored but unread): depth 0.375. Constant 127 (PortalClippingMode) = 1 selects the portal clip distance: dot((world xyz, 1), portalPlane) with portalPlane = (0, 0, 1, -1/2) is 5/8 - 1/2 = 1/8 at every vertex, so the clip distance keeps the whole triangle (a wrong sign or operand would clip it away).

name: manual-vertex-fetch-null-buffer-defaults
no_effect: Zero instance and view constants give a degenerate position: the primitive covers no fragment, so the render target keeps its authored bytes.
rationale: Function constant 132 enables manual vertex fetch. Every zero-initialized embedded vertex-buffer pointer is null, so each AIR guard bypasses its table lookup and supplies the defined default attribute. Slot zero is the exact same-library invalid-format callback that supplies the table's required type but is unreachable. Clipping is disabled by function constant 35; its only structural backedge is additionally capped by an unsigned 16-bit counter reaching 32. Zero transform constants produce a deterministic degenerate position. Buffer 30 and its reflected offset-zero device buffer are now authored explicitly; the invalid-format callback deterministically supplies the same default attribute when that first record is reached.

name: linked-single-unit-reduce-argmax
rationale: One invocation reduces one float element and writes its zero index. Reduction, broadcast, minor, major, outer-axis, per-thread, and NDArray extents and strides are one, bounding every loop to the single authored value.

name: depth-of-a-multisampled-fragment-only-where-its-stencil-passes
rationale: A per-pixel [[stencil]] output (word x of buffer 0: ['0x10', '0x50', '0x3f', '0x40']) beside a [[depth(any)]] output (float x of buffer 2: [0.25, 0.75, 0.125, 1.0]) in a pass of 4 samples, over a depth attachment of 0.5 in every sample under depth compare always with depth writes on (a state whose stencil write cannot depend on the depth result): a sample whose stencil test fails gets no depth. DESIGN D295 (Metal's [[stencil]] semantics as D295.1 measured them, 4x included): the output's low 8 bits r are the reference of both faces; each covered sample's test is (r & readMask) cmp (s & readMask) for its stored s; the face's operation writes (s & ~writeMask) | (op(s, r) & writeMask); a sample that fails the stencil test gets no depth or color; the stencil test precedes the depth test. The pass is multisampled, 4 samples per pixel, and the draw is the executors' fullscreen triangle (1 instance), which covers every sample and is back-facing under the default clockwise winding (case 8db41494), over a 4x1 stencil attachment whose every sample holds 0x40 (a multisampled stencil is authored uniform and cleared to it). The back face's state: compare less, stencil failure keep, depth failure replace, pass replace, read mask 0xFF, write mask 0xFF; the front face's (compare always, stencil failure zero, depth failure zero, pass zero, read mask 0xFF, write mask 0xFF) would give other values. The encoder's references are 0 and unused. Predicted depth, pixel by pixel, 4 samples each: [0.25, 0.25, 0.25, 0.25, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.125, 0.125, 0.125, 0.125, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5]. On a device without VK_EXT_shader_stencil_export the engine tests and writes each sample in the shader under the ordered pixel interlock against a multisampled shadow of the attachment, keeping the passing samples in its sample mask. The observation is every sample of the whole depth attachment, pixel by pixel, sample by sample. The AIR has no loop.

name: histogram-three-channels-past-the-top-bin
rationale: The three-channel loop is a fixed trip count of three, so the dispatch is bounded by the AIR itself. minTexture is (2,0,1) and maxTexture is (10,8,9), so every denominator is exactly 8 and every bin count exactly 4: the scaled index is (val - lo)/2, exact for these integers. The chosen texels drive each of the three arms of the index math at once - an exact zero, two half-integers that must truncate down rather than round (1.5 to 1 and 2.5 to 2), and an exact 4 that lands one past the top bin so air.clamp.u.i16 has to pull it back to 3. maskTexture is zero at (0,1), so that thread returns before reading anything and contributes nothing. The nine surviving atomic adds are order-independent, so the twelve-bin device buffer must read back 1,0,1,1,0,1,1,1,1,1,0,1.

name: indexed-patch-draws-a-kernel-encodes-on-a-template-without-control-point-indices
rationale: Indexed patch draws a kernel encodes in an indirect command buffer that allows indexed patch draws alone (DESIGN D336 item 9), each run by the post-tessellation template (token 1, inherited, with the marks buffer the execution binds at vertex index 0): every domain point stores 0x10000 | instance << 8 | patch at its cell of grid instance * 8 + patch. The template's pipeline has no control-point index type, so Metal draws each patch's own control point and reads no control-point index buffer (EVs ICBV-ipatch-m3 and -m4). Triangle factor structures of buffer 3: 1, 1, 2, 1. Thread 0 (device buffers): patches at positions 1 and 2 with indices 5 and 6 (from the second device index), control-point indices from byte 4, two instances from 1, factors from the second structure on (2 and 1), scale 1. Thread 1 (constant buffers): patch index 2, instance 3, factors 1 at scale 2: factors of 2. Thread 2 (no patch index buffer, device control-point indices): patch 0, instance 4, factors 1 at scale 0.5, which integer partitioning rounds up to 1. Thread 3 (neither index buffer): patch 2, instance 5, factors 2. Expected nonzero words: 325: 0x10105, 327: 0x10105, 329: 0x10105, 331: 0x10105, 335: 0x10105, 337: 0x10105, 345: 0x10105, 350: 0x10106, 354: 0x10106, 370: 0x10106, 525: 0x10205, 527: 0x10205, 529: 0x10205, 531: 0x10205, 535: 0x10205, 537: 0x10205, 545: 0x10205, 550: 0x10206, 554: 0x10206, 570: 0x10206, 650: 0x10302, 652: 0x10302, 654: 0x10302, 656: 0x10302, 660: 0x10302, 662: 0x10302, 670: 0x10302, 800: 0x10400, 804: 0x10400, 820: 0x10400, 1050: 0x10502, 1052: 0x10502, 1054: 0x10502, 1056: 0x10502, 1060: 0x10502, 1062: 0x10502, 1070: 0x10502; every other word stays 0.

name: manual-half4-fetch-at-an-offset-transformed-onto-three-of-four-pixels
rationale: Reaching variant of this entry's manual-vertex-fetch case (TODO 6.2, WP-RVC), whose zero constants gave a degenerate position. Constant 132 enables manual fetch; table slot 0 holds the same-library callback re::vertexfetch::fetchFromHalf4, and record 0 of the vertex-argument buffer (15 records of 24 bytes, the rest null) points at half4 positions with stride 8 and offset 8, which skips a leading decoy vertex (40, 40, 40). The three positions are (-1, -1), (3, -1), (-1, 3) with z = 1/4 with the matrix z scale 2, so world z = 5/8. The instance matrix (objectToCrWorld, column-major) scales x and y by 1/2, scales z and translates by (-1/4, -1/4, 1/8); crWorldToProjArray[0] keeps x, y and w and maps z to z/2 + 1/16, so the clip triangle is (-3/4, -3/4), (5/4, -3/4), (-3/4, 5/4) at w = 1. It covers the pixel centres (-1/2, 1/2), (-1/2, -1/2) and (1/2, -1/2) of the 2x2 target with a margin of at least 1/4 from every edge and misses (1/2, 1/2): pixel (1, 0) keeps its fill. The depth is the same at all three vertices, so its interpolation is exact; every product and sum is a small dyadic value, exact in float with or without contraction, and the observer writes (x + 1/2, y + 1/2, z, 1) for each covered pixel. This entry applies no depth bias (screenSpaceDepthBias = 1/4 is authored but unread): depth 0.375. Constant 127 (PortalClippingMode) = 1 selects the portal clip distance: dot((world xyz, 1), portalPlane) with portalPlane = (0, 0, 1, -1/2) is 5/8 - 1/2 = 1/8 at every vertex, so the clip distance keeps the whole triangle (a wrong sign or operand would clip it away).

rationale: Two threads split a 4x2 rgba32_sint image by column parity, each folding its four texels' int2 with air.min.s.v2i32 and air.max.s.v2i32 into threadgroup memory; threads 0 and 1 then reduce component 0 and component 1 across both entries. name: copy-a-struct-prefix-out-of-a-uniform-into-two-locals
rationale: An llvm.memcpy whose LENGTH is shorter than the source object is a PREFIX copy, and the emitter has to rebuild it out of typed access chains because SPIR-V logical addressing has no byte copy. Five emitter rules carry that shape -- emit_prefix_source_struct_memcpy, emit_aggregate_memcpy, struct_prefix_fields_compatible, emit_prefix_struct_memcpy and emit_prefix_array_memcpy -- and no authored case reached any of them, while 44, 40, 38, 22 and 13 corpus sources do. The AIR is hand-written because every corpus host that reaches all five in one module is a 300-line texture/atomic/threadgroup pipeline whose answer cannot be driven to exact bytes. Buffer 0 is Params { Row { float v[4]; float tail; }; Cfg { Pair { float f; int i; }; float tail; }; }. The first memcpy copies 16 of Row's 20 bytes into a [4 x float] local: the destination type does not match the source struct, so the copy descends to source field 0 and becomes a four-element array copy. The second copies 8 of Cfg's 12 bytes into a Pair local: the same descent, then a two-field struct copy that has to place the float at offset 0 and the int at offset 4. Threads 0 through 3 read the local array, thread 4 the pair's float and thread 5 its int widened to float, so the answer is (1, 2, 4, 8, 3.5, 7) and every value is an exact binary32. Copying the WHOLE source object instead of the prefix, or descending one field too far, writes the decoys Row.tail = 999 or Cfg.tail = 555 into a slot; swapping the pair's two members writes 7 at lane 4 and 3.5 at lane 5; dropping either copy leaves an undefined local.

name: outline-a-picked-object-from-eight-neighbour-indicators
rationale:
outlineRetina_frag draws a selection outline: it samples eight neighbours of one texel of a picked-object buffer, turns each of six neighbour pairs into a zero-or-one indicator, thresholds four of the samples, and combines them into a two-component gradient whose length is the outline strength. The indicators are `air.convert.f.v3f16.u.v3i1` and `air.convert.f.v4f16.u.v4i1` -- the whole shader is those two conversions feeding arithmetic, so a lowering that produced anything but 1.0 and 0.0 from an i1 vector would move every pixel.

Each `air.mix.v3f16` here reduces to an exclusive or. Its first two arguments are an indicator and its complement, so `mix(e, 1-e, z)` is `e` when the third indicator is zero and `1-e` when it is one -- the case is what pins that the conversion of a negated comparison really is the complement, and not, say, a sign or a mask.

A fragment case cannot choose its varyings, but a nearest, normalized, clamp-to-edge constexpr sampler over a texture the size of the render target maps pixel px to texel px, and the eight neighbour offsets are texel offsets the sample call carries directly. On a four-by-four target every pixel is on a border, so all eight offsets exercise the clamp. The harness's vertex shader runs `uv.y` opposite to the framebuffer, so pixel row py reads texture row H-1-py; the expectation is derived through that, and a case that had it backwards would disagree at twelve of the sixteen pixels.

The colour values are drawn from 0, 1, 2 and 4, which makes every comparison exact and gives the `== 0` tests real work: zero is both the value the indicators test for and the value below the 0.002 threshold, so the two tests separate. The gradient components are then small integers, and the table was drawn until the squared length is a perfect square at every one of the sixteen pixels is either a perfect square below sixteen or at least sixteen -- in the first case `air.sqrt.f16` returns an exact integer and the quarter-scale is exact, and in the second the quarter-scaled length is at least one, so the `fmin` against one returns one whatever the square root did with the last bit. The remaining constants, 0.89990234375 and 0.0999755859375, are both exact in binary32 and so are their products with the outline strength, so a contraction of the multiply and add into an FMA cannot change the answer.

The depth half is the other conversion, `air.convert.f.f32.u.i1`. The shader takes the minimum of a three-by-three neighbourhood of the picked-depth buffer against a starting value of one, biases it by a millionth, and compares the scene depth against it; the two depth tables are drawn from values a tenth apart, so the bias cannot flip the comparison, and both arms occur in the same dispatch.

name: a-nan-loses-to-a-number-in-four-plain-symbols
rationale: Metal specifies plain fmin/fmax NaN-aware -- one NaN operand loses to the other, two give a NaN -- and clamp and saturate inherit it, so a NaN clamps to the FLOOR rather than to zero. This case reads both NaNs from a buffer so nothing folds, pins 3.0 for all four min/max orderings, 2.5 for both NaN clamps against a non-zero floor, 0.0 for saturate, and only is-a-NaN for the two-NaN answer, whose payload Metal takes from the second operand and which no implementation owes.
